title: Runaway Process Detection (CPU Hog)
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'Runaway Process Detection (CPU Hog)' only. Does not supplant cross-domain SIEM playbooks for unrelated domains or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `linux_capacity_exceptions.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `linux_runaway_process_detection_cpu_hog` (UC-1.1.84), SOC dashboard panel "Linux — Runaway Process Detection (CPU Hog)", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:linux_controls.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=os` sourcetype='top' that satisfy the UC-1.1.84 SPL filters for 'Runaway Process Detection (CPU Hog)'. Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `os` / `top` events outside the detection threshold, or exclude the test entity via `linux_capacity_exceptions.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-1.1.84.

dataSources: `sourcetype=top` (Splunk_TA_nix per-process CPU fields) Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
spl:
index=os sourcetype=top host=*
| stats avg(cpu_pct) as avg_cpu by host, process
| where avg_cpu>80
description: Averages per-process **cpu_pct** from `top` samples in the search window and flags **(host,process)** pairs above an **80**% average—tune to your workload class.
value: A single hot process on a shared host can starve others even when **vmstat** still looks “OK”; `top` granularity is the fastest path to the binary name for support teams.
implementation: Field may be **pctCPU** or **pcpu** depending on TA version—normalize in **props**. Add `| where count>10` on underlying events to require enough samples before paging.
cimSpl: | tstats `summariesonly` avg(Processes.cpu_load_percent) as avg_cpu from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes by Processes.dest Processes.process_name span=5m | where avg_cpu>80
dataModelAcceleration: Enable **Endpoint.Processes** acceleration after `top`/`ps` is mapped with **cpu_load_percent** per process (CIM field names may differ—align `Fieldsummary` first).

references.title: Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Patch Tuesday / unattended-upgrades** — CPU and disk I/O spike during package application for 'Runaway Process Detection (CPU Hog)'. Correlate with apt/yum logs in same window.

2. **Nightly backup or log-rotate job** — Predictable I/O burst on fixed cron schedule.

3. **Synthetic monitoring probe** — Nagios/Zabbix agent generates periodic load.

4. **New host onboarding** — Baseline metrics unstable first 48h on `os` `top`.

**Suppression mechanism:** `linux_capacity_exceptions.csv` keyed on `host`, `valid_until`.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• `top` script enabled; confirm **cpu_pct** exists with a short **Fieldsummary**.

**CIM** — If `Processes.cpu_load_percent` does not exist in your build, adjust `cimSpl` to the field your **CIM** engineer published for per-process CPU.


Step 3 — Validate
Run `top` or `htop` on the host and **pidstat** for one-minute **CPU** proof; compare the **process** string to Splunk (watch for **truncation**).

Step 4 — Operationalize
Use the same panel next to the **CPU utilization trending** host-level UC for context.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (`Splunk_TA_nix` — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=top into os. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`avg_cpu, host, process`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: We help you spot one program that is eating most of the processor for a while, so you can stop it or fix it before everything else on the machine feels slow.
